summary: Two clients on a NIFTY future: an LTP holder, then a Depth 20 subscribe (acknowledged as 5) moves the ticker to full by subscribing it again; one full packet serves both, the book with its OI; the Depth holder leaving moves it back to ltp, whose packets carry no time.

notes: Vortex replaces a ticker's mode when it is subscribed again; both sides send one subscribe at the new mode and no unsubscribe.

deviations.reason: The desktop sends the canonical price_change and price_change_percent on an instrument beside the web adapter's own change keys (change, change_percent); the adapter sends no price_change, which is not a docs key, so it goes. Open until wire's per-broker rule for canonical keys (each key's mode range or never, index and non-index apart; lead 2026-11-09).

Market-state rule (lead 2026-11-09: the previous close overlays in the snapshot). An ltp packet carries no previous close. The bridge keeps the instrument's last known close within one connection (feed/bridge/snapshot.rs, audit C03) and works the change out again from the new price, so the LTP frame carries the close and change the full packet brought; the web's frame from an ltp packet has none (the Rupeezy adapter keeps no snapshot). Every value is the broker's.

deviations.reason: The web sends null; the docs say leave it out (lead decision 2026-11-09, 4(c)): an ltp packet, or an ohlcv packet before the first trade, carries no trade time, so the desktop's frame has no ltt, where the web sends ltt null.
Without a trade time or update time the web sends timestamp null, a market data frame with no time (the SDK reads data.timestamp); the desktop stamps the time the packet was received.
